objective: Prove that for every three-place tiling contact with a constant frame, an odd class has an assignment on its cylinder exactly when some periodic wall crosses the cylinder without colliding with its own copies (necessity through cyclic covers, since the cylinder's assignments form a one-dimensional shift of finite type), and that for the six bending contacts whose walls only move up or left, all odd classes in the open first quadrant contradict together.
status: Proved by WALLS-WITH-CHOICES-20261024-001A-P001 (V1 prose proof, standard-library check passed). For every three-place tiling contact with a constant frame (27 of 30), an odd class has an assignment on its cylinder exactly when some periodic wall crosses that cylinder without meeting its own copies, equivalently when the torus's wall graph has a closed walk with a transverse class and no overlap in Z c + Z e: necessity because the cylinder's assignments form a one-dimensional shift of finite type, so some cyclic cover has an assignment, one of whose walls crosses the loop an odd number of times. The earlier theorems on straight and rotating walls are special cases. For the six bending contacts whose walls move only up or left, all odd classes in the open first quadrant contradict together, exactly when the wall graph has no cycle; contacts whose walls turn both ways can split the first quadrant.
title: The wall theorem: periodic walls decide every direction
